title: AdapterCapabilities

provider.description: A provider's id, as the environment's adapter registry keys it: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (claude).

displayName.description: The provider's name as a client shows it: Claude.

interactivePrompts.description: A run can stop and ask a permission prompt or a question, answered from any client.

partialMessages.description: A run streams assistant.delta fragments; without it only the settled items arrive.

providerQueue.description: The provider holds messages sent during a turn; without it the environment holds them and starts the next run with them when the turn ends.

withdraw.description: The adapter can take back a queued message its provider holds, by id; messages the environment holds can always be withdrawn.

steering.description: The provider folds a queued message into the running turn at its next boundary; presupposes providerQueue.

resume.description: A session's next run resumes the provider's own session.

fork.description: A session can be forked, from its end or from a user message.

rewind.description: A session can be rewound to a user message.

sessionListing.description: The provider's sessions in an account's directory can be listed, and a listed session's history read.

subagents.description: A run delegates work to subagents and background tasks, reported by tasks.changed and stopped by runs.stopTask.

subagentTranscripts.description: A subagent's own transcript can be read on demand.

titleRead.description: The provider generates a session title the environment can read.

titleWrite.description: A user title can be mirrored into the provider's own title field.

transcriptDelete.description: The provider's transcript of a session can be deleted when the session is purged.

planUsage.description: Plan usage can be read per window, with the account's identity.

contextReadings.description: Runs report the latest main request context independently of cumulative token spend.

liveModels.description: The provider's models are listed live; without it the catalogue is the adapter's static list.

commands.description: The provider's slash commands can be listed for an account and workspace without spending tokens.

imageInput.description: A message can carry image attachments.

fileInput.description: A message can carry file attachments.

modeChange.description: A live run's mode can be changed (permissions.mode.set); without it a new mode applies at the session's next run.

containment.description: The adapter enforces a run's containment level through its provider's sandbox (#133, #140); without it only off is available to the runs of its accounts.

kind.description: How an adapter delivers standing instructions to its provider: system-prompt-append (Claude), developer-instructions (Codex), prompt (a local model), or none.

maxCharacters.description: The most characters the channel carries; null when it has no cap.

instructionChannel.description: An adapter's instruction channel: its kind and its character cap.

nativeProjectInstructions.description: The provider loads a trusted repository's own instruction files itself (Claude: CLAUDE.md through its project settings); without it the composer hands it the repository's AGENTS.md, else CLAUDE.md, in the project layer.

items.description: A root of a trusted repository a provider may load itself: .claude/skills or .agents/skills (its skills), or .claude/commands (its own commands). Found in the workspace directory and each parent up to the repository's root.

nativeSkillRoots.description: The roots of a trusted repository the provider loads skills or commands from itself (Claude: .claude/skills and .claude/commands, through its project settings): a member there is native, left out of the generation and hidden, when switched off, the provider's own way.

mode.description: What an agent may do without asking during a run, in the order ceilings use: plan < acceptEdits < auto < bypassPermissions. Claude's default and dontAsk are never used.
What an agent may do without asking during a run, in the order ceilings use: plan < acceptEdits < auto < bypassPermissions. Claude's default and dontAsk are never used.

reason.description: Why the account cannot use the mode, for people.

items.description: Whether an account can use a mode and, when it cannot, why.

modes.description: The modes the adapter maps onto its provider (ADR 0006), each available or not with the reason; a run asking for an unavailable or unlisted mode gets the next lower available one.

description: An adapter's capabilities descriptor: its provider, a flag per optional power, its instruction channel, whether it loads a trusted repository's own instructions itself and which of its skill roots, and its modes.
